concept: A tag labels a thing and does nothing when pressed, so it is etched into the glass instead of standing on it, with shade on its top edge and light on its bottom edge.

root.why: etched into the glass with shade on top and light below, uppercase micro type, so it is never mistaken for a button

neutral.why: a status with no tone, in the grey crystal, for drafts and counts

info.why: the info crystal tints blue so a notice reads as information at a glance

positive.why: the positive crystal tints green so a done state reads as settled

warning.why: the warning crystal tints amber so a state that needs care stands out

critical.why: the critical crystal tints red so a failure is the loudest mark on the pane

accent.why: the accent crystal tints violet for new and featured, a hue no status uses

toned.why: a tag with a tone takes a thin tint of it in the etch, for colour-coded categories that still name themselves

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours drop the etch, so a real system-colour border keeps the shape

default_to_avoid.pattern: a small coloured or outlined pill tag that looks like a button (GitHub labels, Material assist chip)
default_to_avoid.why_not: a raised or ringed pill reads as pressable, and a reader taps a tag that does nothing

derivation.consequence: the whole pane is never a hidden button; actions sit on it as separate objects
derivation.form: a tag is not an object you press, so it is cut into the surface instead of placed on it

derivation.consequence: legibility comes from dimming and blurring the backdrop (brightness, blur) inside a smoked body thick enough that a pane reads as a slab of glass, with the scene softened behind it
derivation.form: the etch is a dimmed patch with shade on top and light below, no opaque fill

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns no hue of its own, only white at opacities and one ink, and colour appears only where it states a status or marks a diagram
derivation.form: tags carry no colour of their own, only the text colour

derivation.consequence: controls are full pills because they are held in the hand
derivation.form: the etch is a pill, the system shape, but small and flat

variants.reason: B is the only one that cannot be mistaken for a button: it sits below the surface (P3 interaction) while buttons stand on it. A is a ringed pill like the shipped one and like a quiet button. C has no shape, so a row of tags reads as loose words.
